exposure: Medical termination of pregnancy for fetal anomaly at or beyond 20 weeks gestation
outcome: Manual removal of retained placental tissue
Severe maternal morbidity (including amniotic fluid embolism, cardiac arrest, major obstetric hemorrhage, uterine rupture, and intensive care unit admission)
cohort: 407 consecutive singleton pregnancies that underwent medical termination of pregnancy for fetal anomaly at or beyond 20 weeks gestation at a quaternary maternity centre in Australia.
finding: The most common complications of medical termination of pregnancy for fetal anomaly at or beyond 20 weeks gestation were manual removal of placenta and postpartum hemorrhage, while severe maternal morbidity was rare.
